elements.name: NASA/JPL Small-Body Database (SBDB) Query API
elements.note: values arrive as strings and are stored here as parsed numbers; a may be negative (hyperbolic) or very large (long-period); tp and epoch are TDB Julian dates; m1/k1 are not valid field names for this endpoint (HTTP 400), M1/K1 are

ephemeris.name: NASA/JPL Horizons
ephemeris.frame: geocentric astrometric ICRF/J2000 RA/Dec, degrees; r and delta in au
ephemeris.note: COMMAND is DES=<designation>;CAP - the ;CAP suffix is required, a bare DES= sends Horizons into a record-index search instead of an ephemeris; a designation that Horizons cannot resolve uniquely falls back once to DES=<SPK-ID>;CAP (recorded per comet in provenance.ephemeris_command)

observations.name: COBS - Comet Observation Database
observations.note: visual and CCD magnitudes are reported separately and never merged

noteworthy.basis: compared this run with data/overhead/comets.json: candidate ids, SBDB element epochs, COBS last measured magnitudes and predicted minimum geocentric distances, using the published thresholds; that artifact was generated 2026-10-20T06:47:41Z

notes: candidate discovery: SBDB comet query sorted by -last_obs, filtered in Python to last_obs >= 2025-06-08 (500-day freshness window) because the SBDB filter language rejects last_obs

ranking uses the IAU total magnitude model M1 + 5*log10(delta) + K1*log10(r) evaluated over the horizon at the daily point where each object is predicted brightest, with r and delta from a local two-body Kepler propagation of the SBDB elements; measured against Horizons for 2P/Encke that propagation is 0.16-0.65 arcmin from the element epoch to +800 days and 4.3 arcmin at +1174 days (missing non-gravitational acceleration and perturbations)
candidate discovery result: 2000 SBDB comet rows, 287 inside the freshness window, 286 rankable, 24 selected (requested 24, hard cap 40; objects brighter than 12 mag are taken first: ['C/2026 O1'])
candidates with unusable elements: C/2025 N1: eccentricity 6.141351449317625 outside [0,5]
published candidates span predicted peak magnitudes 11.89 to 16.76

ephemeris: one geocentric OBSERVER request per published comet over [2026-10-21T00:00:00Z, 2027-04-19T00:00:00Z]; 25 Horizons requests, 24 usable; RA/Dec are astrometric ICRF/J2000 degrees and light-time corrected, exactly as Horizons delivered them

sampling: --step-hours 48 is the requested maximum, but each comet gets the coarsest step from [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 48] h whose linear interpolation stays within 0.02 deg mid-way (the browser interpolates linearly), estimated from the local geometry before the request; steps used: 2P=8h, P/2026 R2=8h, 161P=12h, C/2026 O1=24h, 260P=24h, C/2026 A2=24h, 11P=24h, C/2024 T5=48h, C/2025 Y1=48h, C/2025 V2=48h, C/2025 M2=48h, 10P=48h, P/2026 T1=48h, C/2024 R4=48h, C/2024 J3=48h, 78P=48h, C/2014 UN271=48h, C/2023 R1=48h, C/2026 P2=48h, C/2026 C1=48h, 88P=48h, C/2022 QE78=48h, 123P=48h, 84P=48h
measured worst mid-way interpolation error over all published samples: 0.0178 deg (limit 0.02)
positions are never taken from the local two-body propagation: that model is used only to rank candidates before the ephemeris requests and to sanity-check the committed fixture

observations: COBS obs_list.api over [2026-06-23, 2026-10-21] with exclude_not_accurate=true and exclude_issue=true; visual (obs_type=V) and CCD (obs_type=C) are requested separately (48 requests) and pooled only together with the published per-method counts and ICQ method codes

observation timestamps are the COBS obs_date values, published here as UTC; COBS documents its observation times as UT, but its help page could not be retrieved in this run (HTTP 500) to reconfirm that
the coma diameter is published as arcmin because that is the ICQ convention; the COBS help page could not be retrieved (HTTP 500) to confirm the unit of its coma_diameter field
comets.json carries no ephemeris samples on purpose: it is read on every page load, and the samples live in data/overhead/comet-ephemerides.json

published precision: ephemeris samples carry ra/dec/r/delta to 6 decimals, geometry.min_delta_au to 4 and interpolation_max_deviation_deg to 5; every derived value is computed from the samples as published and the offline validator re-derives it from the artifact with an exact comparison (no rounding tolerance), so the published numbers can never drift from the published samples
COBS API signature versions asserted: obs_list.api 1.5, comet_list.api 1.3
noteworthy comparison against the previous artifact: new_objects=1, brightened=2, faded=0, orbit_updates=0, approaching_minimum_delta=0 (empty lists are the expected steady-state result)

ranking model measured on the published set: the two-body Kepler propagation differs from the Horizons geometry at each predicted peak by at most 3628.2 arcmin (median 2.58 arcmin) and the total-magnitude model evaluated on the propagated geometry differs by up to 1.86 mag; 11 of 24 comets peak more than 2 years after their element epoch, which is where that gap comes from. Published magnitudes always use the Horizons geometry, so this only affects which candidates were selected.
